law.title: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
law.replaces: Indian Penal Code, 1860, for offences committed on or after in_force_from

effective_date_semantics: effective_from and effective_to compare against the date the offence was committed, not the FIR or filing date
dataset_status: draft: records are not production-ready until review.status is verified

relation_types.defined_by: Target section supplies the definition used by this record

relation_types.aggravated_form: Target is the aggravated form of this offence

references.offence_name: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
references.description: Each person is liable for a criminal act done by several persons in furtherance of a common intention as if done by him alone. Cited as 'read with' another chargeable section.

elements.description: Two or more persons involved
A criminal act was done
This accused participated in the act
Common intention shared by all participants

modelling_notes: Applies together with another offence. Evaluate per accused.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 3(5)

references.description: Agreement between two or more persons to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act or a legal act by illegal means.

elements.description: Agreement between two or more persons
Object of the agreement is illegal
Accused is a party to the agreement
Intent to enter the agreement

modelling_notes: May stand alone or be added to another offence. Check whether an overt act is needed when the object is not itself an offence.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 61(2)

references.description: Definition: causing death by an act done with intention of causing death, or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.

elements.description: Death of a person confirmed and cause documented
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Accused's act linked to the death
Intention to cause death or likely-fatal injury, or knowledge of likely death

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 100

references.description: Definition: culpable homicide is murder if done with the intentions or knowledge listed in the section and no exception applies.

elements.description: Death of a person confirmed and cause documented
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Accused's act linked to the death
Intention to cause death, or injury sufficient in ordinary course to cause death, or knowledge the act is imminently dangerous
No exception reducing murder applies (e.g. grave and sudden provocation, private defence)

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 101

references.description: Charge of murder: death caused by the accused's act with the intention or knowledge required for murder.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Death of a person confirmed and cause documented
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Accused's act linked to the death
Intention to cause death, or injury sufficient in ordinary course to cause death, or knowledge the act is imminently dangerous
No exception reducing murder applies (e.g. grave and sudden provocation, private defence)

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 103(1)

references.offence_name: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
references.description: Charge where culpable homicide is established but an exception reduces it below murder, or the intention/knowledge falls short of murder.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Death of a person confirmed and cause documented
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Accused's act linked to the death
Intention to cause likely-fatal injury or knowledge that the act is likely to cause death
Murder threshold not met or an exception applies

modelling_notes: Punishment differs by clause (intention vs knowledge). Capture clause when verifying.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 105

references.description: Death caused by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Death of a person confirmed and cause documented
Rash or negligent act by accused
Accused's act linked to the death
No intention or knowledge of death (not culpable homicide)

aliases: rash and negligent act causing death
modelling_notes: Different punishment rule for registered medical practitioners. Verify clause.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 106(1)

references.offence_name: Causing death by rash and negligent driving and escaping without reporting
references.description: Death caused by rash and negligent driving not amounting to culpable homicide, with the driver escaping without reporting to a police officer or Magistrate soon after.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Death of a person confirmed and cause documented
Accused was driving the vehicle
Driving was rash and negligent
Accused's act linked to the death
Accused left without reporting to police or Magistrate soon after

modelling_notes: New provision. No direct IPC equivalent (verify).

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 106(2)

references.description: Instigating or intentionally aiding a person to die by suicide.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Death by suicide confirmed
Accused instigated or aided the suicide
Instigation or aid linked to the suicide
Intention to instigate or aid

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 108

references.description: Act done with intention or knowledge such that, if death had been caused, the accused would be guilty of murder.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Intention or knowledge such that death, if caused, would be murder
Act capable of causing death in the circumstances
Victim survived (death not caused)

modelling_notes: When hurt results, the section provides a heavier punishment. Capture clause when verifying.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 109(1)

references.description: Definition: causing bodily pain, disease or infirmity to any person.

elements.description: Bodily pain, disease or infirmity documented

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 114

references.description: Charge of voluntarily causing hurt: act done intending or knowing it is likely to cause hurt, and hurt caused.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Bodily pain, disease or infirmity documented
Accused's act linked to the injury
Intention or knowledge that the act is likely to cause hurt

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 115(2)

references.description: Definition: hurt of a kind listed in the section as grievous (for example emasculation, permanent loss of sight or hearing, fracture, severe bodily pain for twenty days).

elements.description: Injury matching a grievous-hurt category documented

modelling_notes: Category list must be encoded as structured sub-elements when verifying.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 116

references.description: Charge of voluntarily causing grievous hurt: act done intending or knowing it is likely to cause grievous hurt, and grievous hurt caused.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Injury matching a grievous-hurt category documented
Accused's act linked to the injury
Intention or knowledge that the act is likely to cause grievous hurt
No grave and sudden provocation

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 117(2)

references.offence_name: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt resulting in permanent disability or persistent vegetative state
references.description: Grievous hurt that causes permanent disability or a persistent vegetative state.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Injury matching a grievous-hurt category documented
Permanent disability or persistent vegetative state documented
Accused's act linked to the injury
Intention or knowledge that the act is likely to cause grievous hurt

modelling_notes: New provision. No direct IPC equivalent (verify).

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 117(3)

references.offence_name: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
references.description: Hurt caused using a dangerous weapon or means (stabbing, cutting, firearm, fire, heated substance, poison, corrosive, explosive).

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Bodily pain, disease or infirmity documented
Dangerous weapon or means used
Accused's act linked to the injury
Intention or knowledge that the act is likely to cause hurt

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 118(1)

references.offence_name: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
references.description: Grievous hurt caused using a dangerous weapon or means.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused performed the act (physical act, weapon use or driving)
Injury matching a grievous-hurt category documented
Dangerous weapon or means used
Accused's act linked to the injury
Intention or knowledge that the act is likely to cause grievous hurt

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 118(2)

references.offence_name: Act endangering life or personal safety of others
references.description: Act done so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others. Higher punishment if hurt or grievous hurt is caused.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Act by accused that endangered life or safety
Act was rash or negligent
Endangerment, accident or injury documented

modelling_notes: Modelled at section level. Clauses for hurt and grievous hurt need separate handling when verifying.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 125

review.notes: Confirm clause structure against official text.

references.description: Voluntarily obstructing a person so as to prevent them from proceeding in a direction they have a right to proceed.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused obstructed the victim
Victim's movement in a direction was prevented
Victim had a right to proceed in that direction

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 126(2)

references.description: Wrongfully restraining a person in a way that prevents them proceeding beyond circumscribing limits.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused restrained or confined the victim
Victim confined within circumscribing limits
Confinement had no legal justification

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 127(2)

references.description: Taking or enticing a minor or a person of unsound mind out of the keeping of the lawful guardian without the guardian's consent.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused took or enticed the person
Victim is a minor or of unsound mind
Victim removed from lawful guardianship
Guardian did not consent

modelling_notes: Models kidnapping from lawful guardianship only. Kidnapping-from-India limb not modelled.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 137(2)

review.notes: Confirm sub-section numbering and age thresholds against official text.

references.description: Dishonestly taking movable property out of a person's possession without consent.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused took or moved the property
Property is movable
Taken without owner's consent
Dishonest intention

modelling_notes: Definition sub-section 303(1) is modelled inside this record.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 303(2)

references.description: Theft or extortion accompanied by, or through, instant death, hurt, wrongful restraint or fear of it.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Theft or extortion of property
Hurt, restraint or fear of instant hurt/death put on victim
Dishonest intention

modelling_notes: Modelled at section level. Sub-sections for definition, punishment and aggravated forms need separate handling.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 309

review.notes: Confirm sub-section numbering against official text.

references.description: Robbery, or attempt to commit robbery, by five or more persons conjointly.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Five or more persons acted conjointly
Robbery committed or attempted
Dishonest intention

modelling_notes: Dacoity with murder and related clauses are separate provisions, not modelled here.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 310(2)

review.notes: Confirm sub-section numbering against official text.

references.description: Dishonest misappropriation or conversion of property by a person entrusted with it or with dominion over it.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Property entrusted to accused or under accused's dominion
Accused misappropriated, converted or disposed of the property
Dishonest intention

modelling_notes: Definition sub-section 316(1) is modelled inside this record. Aggravated forms (clerk, servant, banker) not modelled.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 316(2)

references.offence_name: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
references.description: Cheating by deceiving a person and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver property or to make, alter or destroy a valuable security.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused deceived the victim by false representation
Victim delivered property because of the deception
Dishonest or fraudulent intention at the time of inducement

modelling_notes: Definition sub-section 318(1) is modelled inside this record.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 318(4)

references.description: Threatening a person with injury to person, reputation or property with intent to cause alarm or to compel an act or omission.

Threat communicated by accused
Threat of injury to person, reputation or property
Intent to cause alarm or compel an act or omission

modelling_notes: Threat of death or grievous hurt and anonymous threats are separate sub-sections, not modelled here.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 351(2)

references.description: Death of a woman within seven years of marriage, by burns, bodily injury or otherwise than in normal circumstances, where she was subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry soon before death.

elements.description: Victim is a married woman
Death by burns, bodily injury or otherwise than normal circumstances
Death within seven years of marriage
Cruelty or harassment for dowry documented
Cruelty or harassment soon before the death
Accused is husband or relative of husband

modelling_notes: Definition sub-section 80(1) is modelled inside this record.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 80(2)

references.offence_name: Husband or relative of husband subjecting a woman to cruelty
references.description: Cruelty by the husband or his relative towards a married woman, including wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce her or her relatives to meet property or valuable security demands.

elements.description: Victim is a married woman
Accused is husband or relative of husband
Cruelty or harassment conduct documented
Demand for property/dowry, or conduct likely to cause suicide or grave injury

modelling_notes: Definition of 'cruelty' sits in the next section and is modelled inside this record.

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 85

references.offence_name: Rash driving or riding on a public way
references.description: Driving or riding on a public way so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person.

elements.description: Accused person identified
Accused was driving or riding the vehicle
Driving on a public way
Driving was rash or negligent
Accident, danger or injury documented

source.citation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act 45 of 2023), section 281
